_readme: Copy to ~/.claude/superset-orchestrator/config.json (board doctor does this on first run).
The orchestrator reads this every cycle; the operator owns it. Never rewrite it without saying so.
operator.githubLogin / linearName are used for `--author @me`-equivalent filters and mention scans.

operator.githubLogin also decides whose PRs reach the board. Set it to "*" for every PR in the repo, which is what a team wants; a login watches that one person. board poll and the menu bar app read the same field, so they cannot disagree.

tracker: optional. Omit it and tickets are Linear, built from operator.linearWorkspace — which is what every config written before this block existed means. tracker.kind is matched against a board item's source.kind, and tracker.issueUrl has {key} replaced by the ticket key. A key from a tracker this does not name still shows on the card; it just does not link, because a link built from another tracker's template goes somewhere wrong rather than nowhere.

tracker.kind "markdown" is the built-in backlog: one file per task, committed to the repo, read by board tasks and polled for free. tracker.path is where the files live inside the repo (default .tasks). See reference/markdown-tracker.md. NOTHING may write a task's status — it is the operator's intent, and an agent writing it would be writing to its own branch.

operator.includeReviewRequests: whether PRs you were asked to review (but did not write) join the board. Default true. Set false to keep the board to authored work only — the review-requested query is skipped entirely, so those PRs never enter signals or get cards.

review: the reviews lane — PRs others wrote that await your review, shown on the app's Reviews tab and by board review list. review.prompt is the template board review start hands the review agent, with {url} {repo} {number} {title} {author} {branch} {base} substituted; unset means the built-in comment-only default. review.countsAsNeedsYou folds pending reviews into the menu-bar alert count; default false (the tab badge is the only signal). Dismissals live in reviews-dismissed.json at the orchestrator root, are permanent per PR, and are reversed only by board review undismiss.

preview: optional. The board finds a preview deployment by matching the PR's bot comments. Vercel by default; give preview.patterns to match Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or anything else. First pattern to match wins, so order is preference. An unusable pattern is dropped rather than fatal.
repos[]: one entry per repo you orchestrate. supersetProjectId comes from `superset projects list --json`.
repos[].reviewers: default reviewers assigned when a PR is opened. First entry is the primary.
repos[].localPath: the main clone (not a worktree) — used for branch existence and log checks.

repos[].name must be the CURRENT GitHub name. The website repo was renamed to acme/platform; `gh pr list --repo acme/website` returns [] silently instead of following the rename, so a stale name looks like 'no open PRs'. The git remote may still say website.git — that is fine for push/fetch, but not for gh.
linear.autoUpdate: the only writes to Linear allowed without asking, per cycle.
slack.channels: read-only scan targets. Empty array disables Slack polling entirely.
limits.maxActiveWorkspaces counts dispatched+building+awaiting-approval+fixing (pr-open counts as 0.5). It counts LOCAL items only.

limits.maxActiveCloudSessions is the same count for cloud items, kept separate because the two are different limits: the local cap is this machine's memory (a workspace is a full checkout plus an agent session), and a cloud session costs this machine nothing. The cloud cap is review capacity and the account's rate limit.

cloud: dispatch to Claude Code on the web with `board dispatch --host cloud`. Off by default. fireUrl is a routine's API trigger endpoint; the bearer token lives in the environment variable named by tokenEnv, NEVER in this file. defaultHost picks the host when --host is not passed. One-time setup and the constraints are in reference/cloud-sessions.md.
cadence values are seconds and feed ScheduleWakeup; the orchestrator may tighten them when CI is running.
gates: set any of these to false only if the operator explicitly asks. Defaults are deliberately cautious.
answers: standing decisions the orchestrator may relay to a blocked agent without asking again.
LAYOUT: this file and workspaces/ live at the ROOT (~/.claude/superset-orchestrator/). Per-project state lives in p/<key>/: board.json, briefs/, signals/, events.log, watch.pid.
workspaces/ is deliberately global — it is the agent status inbox, keyed by globally-unique workspace UUID, so board status needs no knowledge of projects.
repos[].key names the per-project directory. Omit it and it is derived from the repo name (acme/platform -> acme-platform).
Select a project with SUPERSET_ORCH_PROJECT=<key>. With exactly one repo configured it is assumed. With more than one, the board CLI refuses rather than guess.
limits.maxActiveWorkspaces is GLOBAL across every project, not per project. Each workspace is a full checkout plus an agent session, so memory runs out before the number does.
limits.recentlyClosedDays: how long a terminal item (closed/rejected/abandoned) stays on the board, listed under Recently closed, before board archive moves it to archive.json. Default 7.
board watch --install --all installs one poller service per configured project. Separate processes, so one hung cycle cannot stop the others.

review.prompt: You are reviewing a pull request you did not write: {url} — "{title}" by {author}. The PR branch {branch} (into {base}) is checked out in this workspace. Read the full diff commit by commit, run the tests the change touches, and verify the change does what the PR claims. Leave your findings as comments on the PR itself (gh pr review / gh pr comment), specific, citing files and lines. If the change is in a good state — it does what it claims, the tests pass, and you found nothing that must change — approve it (gh pr review --approve), summarising what you checked. NEVER use --request-changes: raise concerns as comments and leave the verdict open — a block is the operator's call, not yours. Never push to this branch and never merge.

answers.prBodyStyle: What changed, why, how it was verified, screenshots for anything visual. Direct, brief and succinct, per the simple-english skill: active voice, one fact per sentence, no padding words, measurable results rather than adjectives.
answers.visualIntent: The operator's screenshots are the source of truth. If none exist for this item, ask.
